name: MMLU-Pro
description: 12,000 multiple-choice questions across 14 academic subjects, with ten answer options to make guessing harder than the original MMLU.

name: GPQA Diamond
description: 198 graduate-level biology, physics and chemistry questions written to be hard to look up, even for skilled non-experts with web access.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
description: Expert-written questions at the frontier of human knowledge across dozens of subjects. Scores here are without tools.

name: AIME 2025
description: The 30 problems of the 2025 American Invitational Mathematics Examination; answers are integers, so there is no partial credit.

name: MATH-500
description: A 500-problem subset of the MATH competition dataset, spanning algebra to number theory.

name: SWE-bench Verified
description: 500 real GitHub issues from popular Python repositories, human-verified as solvable; the model must produce a patch that passes the tests.

name: LiveCodeBench
description: Competitive-programming problems collected continuously after model training cutoffs, to limit contamination.

name: Terminal-Bench
description: End-to-end tasks an agent completes in a real terminal: building software, configuring systems, analyzing data.

name: τ²-bench (Retail)
description: Simulated customer-service conversations where the agent must follow policy while using tools to resolve requests.

name: MMMU
description: College-level questions that require understanding images such as charts, diagrams and photos across 30 subjects.

name: MRCR (128K)
description: Multi-round co-reference resolution: find and reproduce specific earlier turns hidden in a ~128K-token conversation.

name: LMArena Text
description: Elo rating from crowdsourced, blind, head-to-head votes on which response people prefer.
